# Server-side request to a URL from HTTP request data (Node.js)

`qualor:js/ssrf` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-918](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/918.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A01:2025 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A01_2025-Broken_Access_Control/), [A10:2021 Server-Side Request Forgery](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A10_2021-Server-Side_Request_Forgery_%28SSRF%29/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
Outgoing HTTP requests whose server is decided by the incoming request: the URL given to `fetch()`,
undici, axios, got and Node's `http`/`https` modules, when request data forms the whole URL, its
scheme or its host. This includes request data after an origin without a trailing `/`
(`'https://api.example.com' + x`, where `@evil.example` names another host).
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
The request leaves from the server, inside your network. A client who picks the server can make it
call internal services, admin interfaces or the cloud metadata endpoint
(`http://169.254.169.254/`), which may hand out credentials, and read the answers if the server
passes them on.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the URL to fetch comes from the query string.

```javascript
const express = require('express');

const app = express();

app.get('/preview', async (req, res) => {
  const response = await fetch(req.query.url);
  res.json({ status: response.status });
});
```

**Compliant:** the origin is fixed and ends with `/` before any request data.

```javascript
const express = require('express');

const app = express();

app.get('/preview', async (req, res) => {
  const response = await fetch('https://api.example.com/users/' + encodeURIComponent(req.query.id));
  res.json({ status: response.status });
});
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep the origin fixed and end it with `/` before any request data:
  `'https://api.example.com/users/' + id`. Encode path segments with `encodeURIComponent()`.
- Or give relative paths to a client with a fixed base URL (`axios.create({ baseURL })`).
- If the client must choose the server, map its value to a URL through an allow-list.
- Block private and link-local addresses at the network level as well.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Express
- Next.js
- Fastify
- fetch()
- Node.js http
- axios
- Got
- undici

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- An allow-list check of the parsed host before the call
  (`if (!ALLOWED.has(new URL(x).hostname)) return`) is not recognised; allow-list lookups that
  yield constants are.
- A URL built in a variable first is taken as safe only when it starts with a recognisable fixed
  origin (an upper-case constant, `process.env`, a config object, a `const` literal with a host)
  followed by a path separator; concatenations of more than six parts are not checked.
- After a start that does not fix the host, only the next part or two are checked: a second
  constant in between (`'https://' + HOST + ':' + x`) hides the request value.
- An allow-list lookup is recognised only in a `const` table with literal keys and values in the
  same file.
- Request handlers are recognised by the name of their second parameter (`res`, `reply`, `ctx`,
  `next`, ...): a handler written as `(request, out)` is not checked.
- Handlers that destructure the request are followed (`({ query }, res) => ...`,
  `const { body: { name } } = req;`), except a field with a default value in the parameter list
  (`({ query = {} }, res)`), which is not checked.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test files [`rules/js/ssrf/ssrf.js`](../../../rules/js/ssrf/ssrf.js) and [`rules/js/ssrf/ssrf.ts`](../../../rules/js/ssrf/ssrf.ts) hold every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.
